content:
I'm very pleased to announce that – as well as the previously-announced public debate – all of the talks tomorrow at the Swiss Mathematical Society meeting Formalization and proof assistants will be live-streamed via Zoom, including a talk by Fields Medallist @Maryna Viazovska.

The programme is as follows:

  • 2026-03-27T10:00:00+01:00 Maryna Viazovska (EPFL) "The sphere packing problem"
  • 2026-03-27T11:15:00+01:00 Sidharth Hariharan (Carnegie-Mellon), "Formalizing sphere packing"
  • 2026-03-27T13:15:00+01:00 Auguste Poiroux (Math, Inc), "Autoformalization of strong PNT" (mini-talk)
  • 2026-03-27T13:30:00+01:00 Public debate (introduced and chaired by me)
  • 2026-03-27T14:30:00+01:00 Floris van Doorn (Bonn), "Lean – Collaboration via Formalization" (colloquium talk)

The zoom link is:

https://fernuni.zoom.us/my/davidloeffler

Eric Wieser said:

Will any of these be recorded?

... and posted to Youtube or some other publicly available website/repo?

content:
Eric Wieser said:

Will any of these be recorded?

Thanks, Eric, for raising this point. The talks will be recorded and made available via SwitchTube (an academic video sharing website run by a consortium of Swiss universities).

Eric Wieser said:

Will any of these be recorded?

Recordings of the talks are now available here: https://tube.switch.ch/collections/66CerlbmQD

(The discussion about the community impact of AI-company formalization projects was deliberately not recorded, in order to encourage a freer debate; but the talks were all recorded in full, except for a few minor technical glitches.)
Thank you! Will the other talks from this workshop also be available?

Sadly, the debate was, I thought, the whole point of announcing this here #general > The role of AI companies in large formalisation projects. Not everyone is in a timezone where watching such a talk live is possible.. Did anyone take notes from the livestreamed debate?

David Michael Roberts said:

Did anyone take notes from the livestreamed debate?

I can offer my subjective summary of the debate:
The format was Auguste Poiroux answering questions from the audience.
Most of it was just questions from people interested in Lean AI companies, that seem unrelated to the debate (it followed a talk about Math-inc).
When it came to the actual topic of the Zulip thread it kinda felt unfair to criticize Auguste Poiroux for the actions of Math-inc, so while the bad consequences of the sphere packing formalization did come up for a bit, the response was "yeah that sucks".
Basically the debate couldn't actually be a debate, and you didn't miss anything IMO. The debate should probably be with CEOs, to e.g. talk about the coffee meeting from this blogpost.
Though I appreciate the effort of both David Loeffler and Auguste Poiroux in organizing this as a reaction to the Zulip discussion.

Of course, this is just my personal perception of what happened.

I think that's a fair summary, I made a similar comment in private that personally I'd love to see the same kind of debate but in a panel format perhaps, or even in a longer format, or even just done again and with more back and forth. But Auguste managed himself well.

I had to leave early. I brought up the issue of misformalization, and then asked the question of how many human hours were spent to check (for d=8, although I wouldn't mind knowing also for d=24) the result to make sure the output was not misformalized. (Or how many hours to check that it was correct. ) Did an answer to that question appear?
sender_full_name: J. J. Issai (project started by GRP)
